status: AI draft v0.1: not reviewed, not approved for use on any engagement

areas.title: Property, plant and equipment
areas.objective: evidence that assets exist, are owned, are completely recorded, are carried at appropriate amounts after depreciation and impairment, and are properly disclosed.

procedures.text: Obtain the asset register and a movement schedule by class: opening, additions, disposals, depreciation, closing. Check arithmetic and agree to the trial balance and prior-year closing figures.
Select additions and agree to supplier invoices, confirming the amount, the date, that the invoice is addressed to the entity, and that the item is capital in nature.
Physically inspect a selection of assets from the register. For vehicles and property, inspect registration or title documents in the entity's name.
Review repairs and maintenance and similar expense accounts for items that should have been capitalised.
Select disposals and agree to sale documents and proceeds received. Recalculate the gain or loss. Ask whether any assets were scrapped or are no longer in use.
Assess whether useful lives, residual values and depreciation methods are reasonable and consistently applied. Recalculate depreciation in total by class and compare with the charge.
Consider whether there are indicators of impairment, such as idle assets, damage, losses or a decline in the business. If so, examine management's impairment assessment.
Confirm disclosures: policy, reconciliation of movements by class, assets pledged, and capital commitments.
Select assets seen on the premises and trace them to the register.
For assets constructed by the entity or built over time, test the costs capitalised and the date depreciation began. Confirm the treatment of borrowing costs follows the framework.
Where assets are carried at a revalued amount, or impairment has been tested, evaluate the valuation: the valuer's competence and objectivity, the method, and the key assumptions.
Examine large additions near the period end and purchases from related parties: confirm delivery, existence and price.

areas.title: Intangible assets
areas.objective: evidence that intangible assets meet the framework's recognition criteria, exist, are owned, and are carried at appropriate amounts after amortisation and impairment.

procedures.text: Obtain a movement schedule by class, check arithmetic, and agree to the trial balance and prior year.
Agree additions to invoices, contracts or purchase agreements, and confirm the entity holds the rights.
For each class, conclude whether recognition is permitted by the framework, paying particular attention to internally generated items and development costs.
Assess the useful lives and recalculate amortisation.
Consider indicators of impairment, including whether each asset is still in use and generating benefit.
Confirm disclosures: policy, useful lives, movement reconciliation.
For goodwill or assets acquired in a business combination, examine the purchase agreement, the allocation of the price, and the amortisation or impairment treatment.
Where capitalised costs are significant, test the underlying costs in detail, such as timesheets and contractor invoices, and challenge the evidence of future benefit.

areas.title: Investments and other financial assets
areas.objective: evidence that investments exist, are owned, are measured as the framework requires, and that income from them is complete.

procedures.text: Obtain a schedule of investments with movements. Agree to the trial balance.
Inspect share certificates, registers, custodian statements or agreements, or confirm holdings directly with the custodian or investee.
Agree purchases and sales to contracts and bank. Recalculate gains and losses.
Conclude on classification and measurement basis under the framework. For quoted investments, agree prices to an independent source.
For unquoted investments and investments in subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures, obtain the investee's latest financial statements and consider impairment.
Agree dividend and interest income to supporting evidence and assess completeness against holdings.
Confirm disclosures, including whether consolidated statements are required or an exemption applies.
Where fair value is estimated, evaluate the method, the data and the significant assumptions, and consider developing your own estimate or range.

areas.title: Inventories
areas.objective: to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that inventories exist, are owned, are complete, are measured at the lower of cost and the framework's recoverable measure, and are properly disclosed.

procedures.text: Obtain the final inventory listing by item with quantity, unit cost and value. Check its arithmetic and agree the total to the trial balance.

Where inventory is material, attend the physical count. Evaluate management's count instructions, observe that they are followed, and inspect the condition of goods. If attendance is impracticable, perform alternative procedures and record why.
At the count, perform test counts in both directions: from the count sheets to the floor, and from the floor to the count sheets. Record the items for later tracing.
Trace your test counts and a selection of count sheets into the final inventory listing. Investigate differences.
If the count was held on a date other than the period end, test the roll-forward or roll-back of movements between the two dates.
Record the last goods-received and dispatch documents at the count. Confirm that purchases and sales either side are recorded in the correct period and consistent with what was counted.
Test unit costs for a selection of items to supplier invoices, and confirm the cost formula used is permitted and applied consistently.

Test for write-downs: compare cost with selling prices after the period end less costs to sell for a selection, and review ageing or last-movement reports for slow-moving items. Assess management's allowance.
Ask about, and look for evidence of, goods held on behalf of others, consignment stock, and goods held at third-party locations. Confirm third-party holdings directly or inspect them.
Confirm disclosures: policy, cost formula, carrying amounts by category, write-downs, and inventory pledged as security.
For manufactured goods, test the build-up of cost: materials, labour and overheads. Confirm overhead absorption is based on normal capacity and excludes selling and administration costs.
Analyse inventory days and gross margin by product line against the prior year. Investigate unexpected movements.
Compare last year's write-down allowance with what was actually sold or scrapped.
Test the accuracy of the ageing or last-movement report used for the write-down assessment.
Extend count coverage: attend all significant locations, increase test counts, and open sealed packages or check for hollow stacks on a sample basis. Consider unannounced counts.
For high-value items, verify identity and quality, using an expert where the nature of the goods needs one.
Review adjustments made to inventory records after the count and journals posted to inventory near the period end.

areas.title: Trade and other receivables
areas.objective: to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that receivables exist, are owed to the entity, are complete, are recorded in the correct period, are carried at a recoverable amount, and are properly classified and disclosed.

procedures.text: Obtain the customer-by-customer listing with ageing at the period end. Check its arithmetic and agree the total to the trial balance and the lead sheet. Investigate reconciling items.
Compare the balance, the ageing profile and debtor days with the prior year and with your expectation from revenue and credit terms. Obtain and corroborate explanations for unexpected movements.
procedures.evidence: Analytical review with expectation, threshold and explanations

procedures.text: Select balances for external confirmation. Send requests under your own control and have replies come directly to you. Reconcile differences. If confirmation is not used, record why it would be ineffective and what replaces it.
procedures.evidence: Selection basis; requests and replies; reconciliations; control schedule

procedures.text: For selected balances not confirmed or not replied to, and as further evidence for others, trace to cash received after the period end, agreeing to bank statements and to the specific invoices settled.
procedures.evidence: Schedule of post-period receipts tied to invoices and bank

procedures.text: For selected balances with neither a reply nor later receipt, inspect the invoice, the proof of delivery or service completion, and the customer order or contract.
procedures.evidence: Copies or references of documents inspected

procedures.text: Obtain management's assessment of the allowance for doubtful debts. Understand the method, test the ageing it relies on, and consider old balances, disputes, post-period receipts and known customer difficulties. Conclude whether the allowance is reasonable under the reporting framework.
procedures.evidence: Management's calculation; your testing of ageing; your assessment per significant balance

procedures.text: Compare last year's allowance with what was actually collected or written off since, to judge the reliability of management's estimates.
Select sales invoices and credit notes from either side of the period end and agree each to delivery or service evidence, to confirm it is recorded in the correct period.
Review the listing for credit balances, related-party balances, staff and owner balances, and amounts due after more than one year. Confirm each is correctly classified.
For other receivables, prepayments and deposits, obtain a breakdown, agree significant items to supporting documents and recalculate prepaid amounts.
Confirm that the disclosures for receivables, the allowance and its movement, and any balances pledged as security agree to the audit evidence and meet the framework's requirements.
Test the accuracy of the ageing report by tracing a selection of invoices to their dates and confirming they fall in the right ageing band.
Review credit notes issued after the period end and consider whether they reverse sales recorded before it.
procedures.evidence: Listing of post-period credit notes with assessment

procedures.text: For foreign-currency balances, recalculate the translation at the closing rate from an independent source.
Inspect loan agreements, bank letters and board minutes for receivables pledged, factored or assigned.

Extend confirmations to cover a higher proportion of the balance, and include new customers, large balances raised near the period end, and customers with unusual terms. Verify the confirmation address independently of the client's records.
Examine journal entries posted to receivables and revenue near the period end and after it, particularly manual entries and those posted by senior management.
procedures.evidence: Journal selection with support; link to C16

procedures.text: For customers with large or old balances, obtain evidence that the customer is real and able to pay, such as trade licence details, correspondence, and payment history.
Inspect significant contracts and side correspondence for terms that affect when revenue and the receivable should be recognised, such as rights of return or bill-and-hold arrangements.

areas.title: Cash and bank
areas.objective: evidence that cash and bank balances exist, are owned, are complete, and that restrictions and bank facilities are disclosed.

procedures.text: Send confirmation requests, under your control, to every bank the entity dealt with in the period, including accounts with nil balances and accounts closed in the year. Request balances, loans, facilities, security, guarantees and signatories.
Obtain the bank reconciliation for every account at the period end. Check arithmetic, agree the bank balance to the confirmation and statement, and the book balance to the ledger.
Trace reconciling items to bank statements after the period end. Investigate items that did not clear promptly and any old items.
Compare the confirmation replies with the ledger for accounts, loans, guarantees or security not recorded or disclosed.
Where cash in hand is material, count it at or near the period end in the custodian's presence, and reconcile to the ledger. Otherwise review the balance for reasonableness.
Recalculate the translation of foreign-currency balances at the closing rate.
Confirm that overdrafts are shown as liabilities unless offset is permitted, restricted balances and deposits with long maturities are properly classified, and disclosures are complete.

Review large or unusual receipts and payments in the weeks either side of the period end, including transfers between accounts, to confirm they are recorded in the correct period and not recorded twice.
Review reconciliations for other months for unusual items, and confirm they are prepared and reviewed regularly.
Obtain bank statements directly from the bank, or view them through online banking in the client's presence, to confirm the authenticity of statements provided.
Scan bank statements for the whole period for transactions with the owners, related parties or unusual counterparties, and trace them to the ledger.

areas.title: Related-party balances and transactions
areas.objective: to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that related-party relationships and transactions have been identified, accounted for and disclosed as the framework requires, and that they do not conceal fraud or misstate the financial statements.

procedures.text: Starting from the list in B6, remain alert throughout the audit for unlisted related parties. Review bank confirmations, legal correspondence, minutes, significant contracts and the customer and supplier lists for names connected to the owners.
Obtain a schedule of all related-party transactions and balances by party and type. Agree it to the ledger.
Confirm balances directly with each related party, or agree to the counterparty's records where you also audit it. Reconcile differences.
For significant transactions, inspect agreements and supporting documents. Understand the terms, including pricing, interest, repayment and security.
Assess the recoverability of amounts due from related parties, considering the counterparty's financial position and payment history.
Confirm that owner current accounts, loans and trading balances are correctly classified between current and non-current, and between liabilities and equity.
Review expense accounts, particularly travel, vehicle, rent and personal-type costs, for owner's personal expenditure charged to the business.
Obtain details of key management personnel compensation and agree to payroll and other records.

Confirm that disclosures are complete: relationships, transactions, balances, terms, and key management compensation. If the statements say transactions were at arm's length, obtain evidence for that claim.
Obtain written representations that management has disclosed all related parties and transactions and accounted for them properly. Carried to D5.
Compare the pricing and terms of related-party transactions with those of similar transactions with unrelated parties. Note the tax implications for C15.
Search the ledger and bank payments for transactions with newly identified or suspected related parties.

For significant transactions outside the normal course of business, inspect the contracts, evaluate the business rationale, confirm the terms are consistent with management's explanations, and confirm authorisation and approval.

If a related party or significant transaction is found that management did not disclose, tell the team at once, ask management to identify all transactions with that party, ask why it was missed, perform substantive procedures on it, and reconsider the risk assessment and the reliability of management's representations.

areas.title: Trade and other payables, accruals
areas.objective: evidence that all liabilities at the period end are recorded, at the correct amounts, in the correct period, and properly classified.

procedures.text: Obtain the supplier-by-supplier listing with ageing. Check arithmetic and agree to the trial balance.
Compare the balance, creditor days and the list of major suppliers with the prior year and with purchases. Investigate suppliers with unexpectedly low or nil balances.
For major suppliers, selected by volume of purchases and not by balance, reconcile supplier statements to the ledger. Where no statement is available, request confirmation.

Search for unrecorded liabilities: review payments made and invoices received after the period end, up to a date close to the audit report, and confirm that those relating to the period were recorded or accrued.
Review goods-received records for the last days of the period for deliveries not yet invoiced, and confirm they were accrued.
Obtain the accruals schedule. Compare with the prior year and with recurring expenses to identify missing accruals. Test significant items to later invoices or payment and recalculate.
Review for debit balances, related-party balances, and amounts due after one year. Confirm classification and disclosures.
Recalculate the translation of foreign-currency balances at the closing rate.
Review open purchase orders and unmatched delivery notes at the period end for liabilities not recorded.
Review long-outstanding balances and disputed items, and consider whether amounts written back to income are justified.
Extend the search for unrecorded liabilities: lower the selection threshold, extend the period, and confirm directly with suppliers showing nil or small balances.

areas.title: Borrowings and lease obligations
areas.objective: evidence that all borrowings and lease obligations are recorded, at the correct amounts, correctly split between current and non-current, with finance costs complete and terms disclosed.

procedures.text: Obtain a schedule of borrowings with movements: opening, drawdowns, repayments, interest, closing. Agree to the trial balance.
Agree balances, terms and security to lender confirmations (see C6.01) and loan agreements.
Recalculate interest expense and accrued interest from the terms, or test in total against average borrowings and rates.
Recalculate the split between current and non-current from the repayment schedule.
Read the covenants. Test compliance at the period end using audited figures. If breached, consider classification, disclosure and going concern.
Obtain a list of lease agreements. For each significant lease, read the terms and conclude on its classification and accounting under the framework. Recalculate obligations and expense.
Review minutes, bank confirmations, interest expense accounts and large receipts for borrowings not recorded.
Confirm disclosures: terms, security, maturity, defaults, lease commitments, and guarantees given.
For borrowings with unusual features, such as interest-free owner loans, conversion rights or restructured terms, evaluate the accounting against the framework.
Confirm directly with lenders and related parties the absence of other facilities, side agreements or guarantees.

areas.title: Provisions, contingencies and commitments
areas.objective: evidence that all obligations requiring provision are recognised at a reasonable estimate, and that contingencies and commitments are completely disclosed.

procedures.text: Ask management about litigation, claims, disputes, penalties, guarantees, warranties and onerous contracts. Record who was asked and when.
Review legal and professional fee accounts, minutes, and correspondence with lawyers and authorities for indications of claims.
Where litigation or claims are identified or risk is assessed, communicate directly with the entity's external lawyers through a letter of inquiry prepared by management and sent by you.
Obtain a schedule of provisions with movements. For each, understand the basis, test the data, and evaluate the assumptions.
Compare prior-year provisions with actual outcomes.
Identify capital and other commitments from contracts, orders and minutes. Confirm disclosure.
Compare guarantees and contingent liabilities reported in bank confirmations with those disclosed.
For each matter, conclude whether it should be provided for, disclosed as a contingency, or neither, and confirm the disclosures.
For significant estimates, develop your own point estimate or range and compare with management's.
Meet the entity's lawyers, with management's permission, to discuss the likely outcome of significant matters.

areas.title: Employee benefits, including end-of-service benefits
areas.objective: evidence that liabilities to employees are complete and measured as the framework requires.

procedures.text: Obtain the end-of-service calculation by employee. Check arithmetic and agree to the trial balance. Reconcile headcount to payroll records.
For a selection of employees, agree joining date and salary components to contracts and payroll, and recalculate the entitlement under the applicable law and contract.
Conclude whether the measurement method is acceptable under the framework, including whether an actuarial valuation or a permitted simplification applies.
Agree payments to leavers in the year to final settlement documents and bank.
Test the accrual for untaken leave to leave records and salary rates.
Confirm that salaries, bonuses, commissions and statutory contributions unpaid at the period end are accrued. Compare with post-period payments.
Confirm disclosures.
Where an actuary is used, evaluate the actuary's competence and objectivity, test the employee data supplied, and assess the key assumptions.
Test completeness of the employee list by tracing from payroll and visa or labour records to the calculation.

areas.title: Equity and owner accounts
areas.objective: evidence that share capital, reserves and owner accounts are correctly stated, movements are authorised and lawful, and disclosures are complete.

procedures.text: Agree share capital and ownership to the constitutional documents and licence. Inspect evidence for any change in the year.
Prepare or obtain the statement of changes in equity. Agree opening balances to the prior year and each movement to evidence.
Agree dividends or distributions to resolutions and payment. Confirm they were lawful, given available reserves.
Recalculate any statutory reserve transfer required by law or the constitutional documents.
Obtain the movement on each owner's current account. Test significant movements, and conclude on classification between equity and liability. Linked to C7.
Confirm disclosures: capital, reserves and their nature, distributions.
For capital contributions in kind or conversions of loans to equity, examine the agreements, the valuation and the approvals.

areas.title: Revenue
areas.objective: to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence that recorded revenue arose from real transactions, is complete, is measured accurately, is recorded in the correct period, and is properly classified and disclosed.

procedures.text: Obtain a breakdown of revenue by stream and by month. Agree it to the trial balance. For each stream, record the recognition policy and conclude whether it complies with the framework.

Build an expectation of revenue for each stream from independent or audited data, such as volumes and prices, contracts, headcount or capacity. Compare with recorded revenue, set a threshold, and corroborate differences above it.
Select recorded sales and trace each to order or contract, delivery or service evidence, invoice, and receipt of cash.
Select from a source outside the sales ledger, such as delivery notes, job records or contracts, and trace each into recorded revenue.
Test sales and credit notes either side of the period end against delivery or service evidence. Shared with C5.07.
Reconcile revenue per the ledger to revenue reported in VAT returns for the period. Investigate differences.
Confirm that revenue disclosures, including the policy and any disaggregation required, agree to the evidence and meet the framework.
Analyse gross margin by month and by product or customer. Investigate months or lines that depart from the pattern.
For cash sales, reconcile daily sales records or till reports to bankings for selected periods, and observe cash-handling procedures.
For contracts spanning the period end, recalculate revenue recognised from the contract terms and evidence of progress. Assess the reliability of the progress measure.
Test discounts, rebates and returns: agree terms to agreements, recalculate accruals, and review post-period credit notes.

Identify sales recorded in the last weeks of the period that are large, to new customers, or on unusual terms. Obtain evidence of delivery and of the customer's acceptance, and trace to cash received.
Confirm contract terms and the absence of side agreements directly with selected customers.
Test manual journal entries posted to revenue, particularly near the period end. Linked to C16.
For bill-and-hold, consignment, or sales with rights of return, examine the terms and conclude whether recognition is appropriate.

areas.title: Cost of sales and operating expenses, including payroll
areas.objective: evidence that expenses occurred, relate to the business, are complete, are accurately measured, and are recorded in the correct period and account.

procedures.text: Compare each expense line with the prior year and as a percentage of revenue. Set an expectation for significant lines, such as rent from leases and depreciation from the register. Corroborate unexpected movements.
Select expense transactions and agree to invoice, evidence of receipt of goods or services, approval and payment. Confirm business purpose and correct account.
Reconcile cost of sales: opening inventory plus purchases and direct costs less closing inventory. Agree components to C4 and the purchases ledger.
Test purchases cut-off. Shared with C4.06 and C8.05.
Build an expectation of payroll cost from headcount, average pay and changes in the year. Compare with the recorded cost and investigate differences.
Select employees from the payroll and agree to contract, identity or visa record, approved pay rate, and payment to a bank account in the employee's name. Recalculate gross-to-net for one period.
Reconcile total payroll for the period to the ledger and to wage-protection or bank payment records.
Confirm that the classification of expenses is consistent with the prior year and the presentation chosen under the framework.
Test joiners and leavers: confirm that pay starts and stops on the correct dates.
Review sensitive accounts in detail: legal and professional, consultancy, commissions, donations, entertainment, travel and miscellaneous.
Reconcile purchases and input VAT to VAT returns. Linked to C15.

Test for fictitious suppliers or employees: verify a selection of new suppliers independently, look for shared bank accounts or addresses between suppliers and staff, and meet a selection of employees in person.

areas.title: Taxation: corporate tax and VAT
areas.objective: evidence that current and deferred tax and indirect tax balances are complete and accurately calculated under the law, and that disclosures are complete.

procedures.text: Obtain the corporate tax computation. Agree accounting profit to the draft statements and check arithmetic.
Test each significant adjustment to evidence and to the tax law: non-deductible expenses, exempt income, reliefs claimed, losses used, and limits on deductions. Confirm the rate applied.
Confirm that the entity's tax status, registrations and any elections or reliefs relied on are valid and supported, and that conditions are met for the period.
Agree the opening tax balance, payments in the year and prior-year return to tax authority records. Investigate over- or under-provisions.
Identify temporary differences and recalculate deferred tax. Assess whether any deferred tax asset is recoverable.
Reconcile VAT: output and input tax per the ledger to returns filed, and the closing VAT balance to the last return and subsequent payment or refund.
Inspect correspondence with the tax authority for assessments, audits, disputes and penalties. Consider provisions and disclosure. Linked to B5 and C10.
Confirm disclosures: tax expense components, reconciliation of tax expense to accounting profit, and deferred tax.
Evaluate the tax treatment of related-party transactions and whether transfer-pricing requirements and documentation obligations are met. Linked to C7.11.
For uncertain tax positions, evaluate management's judgement, using a tax specialist where needed, and consider provision or disclosure.
Test VAT treatment on a selection of sales and purchases: rate applied, valid tax invoices, and recoverability of input tax.

areas.title: Journal entries and management override
areas.objective: to respond to the risk that management overrides controls to misstate the financial statements.

procedures.text: Understand how journal entries are initiated, authorised and posted, who has access, and whether entries can be changed or deleted after posting. Uses B1.07.
Obtain the full population of journal entries for the period, including post-closing and consolidation-type adjustments. Prove completeness by rolling opening balances forward to closing balances.
Ask staff involved in financial reporting whether they were asked to make unusual entries or noticed inappropriate ones.

Select entries for testing using risk characteristics. Filter the journal listing for: entries at or after the period end; entries posted by senior management or unusual users; round amounts; entries with no description; unusual account pairings, such as revenue against anything other than receivables or cash; entries to seldom-used accounts; entries posted at weekends or outside working hours.
For each selected entry, inspect support, confirm authorisation, and conclude whether it has a valid business reason and is correctly recorded.
Consider whether entries during the period, not only at its end, also need testing, and record the decision.
Review accounting estimates for bias. Consider whether judgements, taken together, lean in one direction, and compare prior-year estimates with outcomes. Uses the retrospective reviews in each area.
Identify significant transactions outside the normal course of business or otherwise unusual. Evaluate whether the business rationale, or lack of one, suggests fraud or concealment.
procedures.evidence: Schedule of unusual transactions with evaluation

procedures.text: Conclude on whether evidence indicates override, and whether the fraud risk assessment needs revising. Report suspected fraud as required.

items.text: For a new client, identify the owners, the beneficial owners and management, and verify their identity as anti-money-laundering rules require.
Consider the integrity of the owners and management, from inquiries, public information and, for continuing clients, past experience.
For a new client, communicate with the previous auditor, with the client's permission, to ask whether there are reasons not to accept.
Confirm the firm has the competence, time and resources to perform the engagement, including any industry or specialist knowledge.
Consider engagement risks: financial difficulty, disputes with previous auditors, unusual pressure on timing or fees, limitations on scope.
For a continuing client, consider matters arising from the previous audit: disagreements, unpaid fees, scope limitations, changes in ownership or business.
Partner concludes on acceptance or continuance before any work starts.
Identify threats to independence: financial interests, business or family relationships, long association, fee dependence, gifts, and employment relationships with the client.
List non-audit services provided to the client, such as bookkeeping, tax, valuation or advisory. Evaluate the self-review and management threats they create and whether each service is permitted.
Record the safeguards applied to each threat, or conclude that the engagement or the service must be declined.
Obtain independence confirmation from each team member.
Partner concludes on compliance with independence requirements. Reconfirm at completion.
Confirm the reporting framework is acceptable.
Obtain management's agreement that it is responsible for preparing the financial statements, for internal control, and for giving the auditor access to information and people.
Issue an engagement letter covering: objective and scope, auditor's and management's responsibilities, the framework, the expected form of the report, and fee and practical arrangements.
For a continuing client, consider whether the terms need revising or the client needs reminding of them.
If management imposes a scope limitation that would lead to a disclaimer of opinion, do not accept the engagement unless law requires it.

checklists.title: Understanding the entity, its environment and its controls

items.text: Record the entity's legal form, licence activities, ownership, management, and those charged with governance. Note whether owners and managers are the same people.
items.evidence: Entity profile; trade licence; ownership chart

items.text: Describe what the business sells, to whom, how it is paid, its main suppliers, its financing, and any significant changes in the year.
Identify the reporting framework and the significant accounting policies. Note any changes in policy and any areas needing judgement or estimates.
Identify external factors: industry conditions, regulation, licensing requirements, tax status, and economic conditions affecting the entity.
Understand how management measures performance, and any targets, bonuses or loan covenants that could create pressure to misstate results.
Understand the control environment: the owner-manager's attitude to controls and record-keeping, competence of accounting staff, and segregation of duties.
Document the accounting system: software used, who can post entries, who can change master data, and how journal entries are initiated and approved.

For each significant transaction cycle (sales, purchases, payroll, cash, inventory if relevant), document how transactions flow from initiation to the ledger, and identify the controls that address risks in that flow.
For controls addressing significant risks, and controls over journal entries, evaluate their design and confirm by inspection or observation that they are in place.
Understand the entity's use of IT: applications relevant to financial reporting, access controls, backups, and any spreadsheets used for key calculations.
Record the sources used: inquiries (who, when), observation, and documents inspected.
Select the benchmark that users focus on most, and record why.
Apply a percentage to the benchmark to set overall materiality. Record the reason for the percentage chosen.
Set performance materiality below overall materiality, reflecting the expected level of misstatement, the control environment and past experience.
Set the amount below which misstatements are clearly trivial and need not be accumulated.
Consider whether any item needs a lower, specific materiality, such as related-party transactions or directors' remuneration.
At completion, reassess materiality against the final figures and revise if the benchmark has moved significantly. Consider the effect on work already done.
Compare each statement line with the prior year and, where available, with budget. Investigate movements above a threshold set from performance materiality.
Compute key ratios: gross margin, debtor days, creditor days, inventory days, current ratio, gearing. Compare with the prior year.
Obtain management's explanations for flagged movements, and note which are unexpected or inconsistent with your understanding of the business.
Carry unexplained or unusual movements into the risk assessment (B8) as potential risks.

Hold a team discussion, led by the partner, on how and where the financial statements could be misstated through fraud, setting aside beliefs about management's honesty. On a single-person engagement, the partner documents this consideration.
items.evidence: Discussion record: attendees, date, matters raised

items.text: Ask management about their assessment of fraud risk, their process for addressing it, and any actual, suspected or alleged fraud.
Ask those charged with governance, where separate from management, and other appropriate staff, the same questions.
Consider fraud risk factors: incentives and pressures, opportunities, and attitudes. Use the factor prompt list.
Treat revenue recognition as a presumed fraud risk. Identify which revenue streams, transactions or assertions give rise to it. If you rebut the presumption, document why.
Treat management override of controls as a significant risk on every engagement. This loads programme C16.
Plan an element of unpredictability in the nature, timing or extent of procedures. Record what it is.
Record the identified fraud risks at the financial statement and assertion levels and carry them into B8 as significant risks.
Identify the laws and regulations with a direct effect on the financial statements, such as company law, tax law and the reporting framework's legal basis.
Identify other laws whose breach could have a material effect or threaten the business, such as licensing, labour, anti-money-laundering and sector rules.
Ask management how they ensure compliance and whether they know of any non-compliance, penalties or regulator correspondence.
Inspect correspondence with licensing and regulatory authorities and the tax authority.
Confirm that licences needed to operate are valid at the period end and the report date.
Obtain from management a list of related parties, the nature of each relationship, and the transactions with them in the period.
Ask how related-party transactions are identified, authorised and recorded.
Compare the list with the prior-year file, ownership records, licence documents and your knowledge of the owners' other businesses.
Share the list with the whole team and instruct them to stay alert for unlisted related parties and for transactions outside the normal course of business.
Assess the risk of undisclosed related parties or transactions, and carry significant ones to B8. This feeds programme C7.
Consider whether events or conditions exist that may cast significant doubt on the entity's ability to continue. Use the indicator list: financial, operating and other.
Ask whether management has made an assessment, what period it covers, and obtain it. If none exists, discuss the basis for using the going-concern assumption.
Where indicators exist, plan the additional procedures for completion (D4) and consider the effect on the risk assessment.

checklists.title: Risk assessment summary and audit strategy

items.text: Identify risks at the financial statement level, those that affect many areas, such as weak record-keeping or a dominant owner-manager. Decide the overall response: staffing, supervision, timing, unpredictability.

For each area and relevant assertion, rate inherent risk as low, moderate or high, considering likelihood and size of misstatement and the inherent risk factors: complexity, subjectivity, change, uncertainty, and susceptibility to bias or fraud.
Flag as significant those risks at the upper end of the scale, all fraud risks, and significant related-party transactions outside the normal course of business.
Decide for each area whether to rely on controls. If so, add tests of controls; if not, record that the approach is fully substantive.
Confirm that every material area has substantive procedures regardless of the assessed risk.
Apply the scoping rule to small areas and record the scoping conclusions.
Record the strategy: scope, timing, team, deadlines, and use of experts or service-organisation reports.
Partner approves the risk assessment and strategy before fieldwork starts.
During the audit, revise the assessment if evidence contradicts it, and record the change and its effect on procedures.
Read the most recent financial statements and the previous auditor's report. Note any modification.
Confirm that the prior year's closing balances have been correctly brought forward.
Confirm that accounting policies are consistent, or that changes are properly accounted for and disclosed.

Obtain evidence on opening balances: review the previous auditor's working papers where permitted, rely on current-year procedures that also cover opening positions, or perform specific procedures on opening inventory, non-current assets and liabilities.
If sufficient evidence on opening balances cannot be obtained, consider the effect on the opinion.
Identify services outsourced that affect financial reporting, such as bookkeeping, payroll, or inventory held by a logistics provider.
Understand the service, its significance, and the controls the entity itself applies over the provider's output.
Decide how to obtain evidence: from records held at the entity, from a report on the provider's controls, or by procedures at or through the provider.
Identify areas where specialist expertise is needed, such as property valuation, actuarial calculations or legal interpretation.
Where management has used an expert, evaluate that expert's competence, capability and objectivity, understand the work, and assess its suitability as evidence.
Where the audit needs its own expert, evaluate competence and objectivity, agree the scope in writing, and evaluate the adequacy of the work.
Accumulate all misstatements identified, other than those clearly trivial, separated into factual, judgemental and projected.
Consider whether the nature or pattern of misstatements suggests that others may exist, and whether the strategy or materiality needs revising.
Communicate all accumulated misstatements to management promptly and ask for them to be corrected.
Record the misstatements corrected, with the journal entries posted.

For uncorrected misstatements, obtain management's reasons, and evaluate whether they are material individually or together, considering size, nature, effect on key lines and ratios, and the effect of prior-period uncorrected items.
Communicate uncorrected misstatements to those charged with governance and ask for correction. Include them in the representation letter.
Conclude whether the statements as a whole are free from material misstatement. If not, see E2.
Perform analytical procedures on the final statements to confirm they are consistent with your understanding of the entity.
Investigate anything unexpected, and consider whether it indicates an unrecognised risk needing further work.

Ask management what procedures they have to identify events after the period end, and whether any have occurred: new borrowings or guarantees, asset sales or losses, litigation, customer failures, changes in ownership.
Read minutes of meetings held after the period end and ask about meetings not yet minuted.
Read the latest management accounts, cash position and bank statements after the period end.
For each event identified, conclude whether it requires adjustment or disclosure.
Perform these procedures up to the date of the auditor's report. Record the date to which the review was performed.
If facts become known after the report date that would have changed the report, discuss with management and follow the required steps.
Evaluate management's assessment: the period covered, the forecasts and their assumptions, and whether it includes all relevant information known to you.
Where events or conditions cast doubt, evaluate management's plans, test the cash-flow forecast and its key assumptions, and consider facts arising since the assessment.
Where the entity depends on support from owners or related parties, obtain written confirmation of the support and evidence of the supporter's ability to provide it.
Ask management about events or conditions beyond the period of their assessment.
Conclude whether a material uncertainty exists and whether the going-concern basis is appropriate.
Confirm disclosures are adequate, and determine the effect on the report. See E1 and E2.
Obtain a representation letter from management with appropriate responsibility, addressed to the auditor.
Confirm it covers management's responsibility for the statements, and that all information and access was provided and all transactions recorded.

Confirm it includes the specific representations required by other standards: fraud, laws and regulations, related parties, subsequent events, going concern, litigation and claims, estimates, and uncorrected misstatements, with the list attached.
Confirm it is dated as near as practicable to, and not after, the date of the auditor's report.
If management refuses, or the representations are unreliable, reconsider management's integrity and the effect on the opinion.

checklists.title: Communication with those charged with governance

items.text: Identify who is charged with governance. Where all of them are also managers, record that matters communicated to management need not be repeated.
Communicate the auditor's responsibilities and the planned scope and timing, at the planning stage.

Communicate significant findings: views on accounting policies, estimates and disclosures; significant difficulties; uncorrected misstatements; representations requested; and other significant matters.
Communicate significant deficiencies in internal control in writing, and other deficiencies to management.
Communicate any identified or suspected fraud or non-compliance with law as required.
Complete the framework disclosure checklist against the final statements.
Check the statements for internal consistency: casting, cross-references, notes to face, and comparatives.
Evaluate overall presentation: whether the statements, including policies and terminology, are understandable and achieve fair presentation.
Confirm all planned procedures are complete, or changes to the plan are recorded with reasons.
Confirm all review points are cleared and all working papers reviewed by someone other than the preparer.
Confirm each significant risk has a documented response and conclusion.
items.evidence: Review of the risk assessment and programmes

items.text: Confirm significant matters, the judgements made and the conclusions reached are summarised for the partner.
Record consultations on difficult or contentious matters and how conclusions were implemented.
Reconfirm independence.
Partner confirms sufficient and appropriate involvement throughout, that sufficient appropriate evidence supports the opinion, and takes responsibility for the engagement.
Confirm the comparatives agree with the prior-period statements or, if restated, that the restatement is properly accounted for and disclosed.
Confirm policies are applied consistently or changes are properly dealt with.
If the prior period was audited by another auditor or not audited, determine the statement required in the report.
If the prior report was modified and the matter is unresolved, determine the effect on the current opinion.
If you become aware of a possible material misstatement in the comparatives, perform additional procedures.

checklists.title: Forming the opinion and the auditor's report

items.text: Conclude whether sufficient appropriate evidence has been obtained and whether uncorrected misstatements are material, individually or together.

Evaluate whether the statements are prepared, in all material respects, under the framework: policies disclosed and appropriate, estimates reasonable, information relevant and understandable, disclosures adequate.
Select the opinion, considering open matters and uncorrected misstatements against materiality. The partner makes the decision.

Generate the report and confirm it contains every required element: title; addressee; opinion; basis for opinion; going-concern section where required; responsibilities of management and those charged with governance; auditor's responsibilities; other reporting responsibilities required by law; name and signature; address; date.
Add any matters that local law requires the auditor to report on.
Date the report no earlier than the date on which sufficient evidence was obtained, including evidence that the statements have been approved by those with authority.

checklists.title: Modified opinions and additional paragraphs (if applicable)

items.text: Identify the cause: the statements are materially misstated, or sufficient appropriate evidence could not be obtained.
Judge whether the effect, or possible effect, is material only, or material and pervasive.
Select the modification: qualified where material but not pervasive; adverse where misstatement is pervasive; disclaimer where the inability to obtain evidence is pervasive.
Draft the basis for modification, quantifying the effect where practicable.
Communicate the expected modification and its wording to those charged with governance before issuing.
Where a material uncertainty about going concern exists and is adequately disclosed, include the required separate section. If disclosure is inadequate, modify the opinion.
Consider whether an emphasis of matter or other matter paragraph is needed, and confirm it is not used as a substitute for a modification.
Determine whether the entity will issue a document containing the audited statements together with other information, such as a directors' or management report.
Read the other information and consider whether it is materially inconsistent with the statements or with your knowledge from the audit.
Resolve inconsistencies with management, and include the required section in the report.
Complete the assembly of the final file promptly after the report date, and within the firm's limit.
During assembly, make administrative changes only: removing superseded drafts, sorting, cross-referencing, signing off completion checklists.
After assembly, lock the file. Nothing may be deleted. Any later addition records who made it, when, and why.
Retain the file for the firm's retention period.
